terraform_note.b_root_and_target_list: Root infra/aws/terraform/ticket-center. The two targets are -target=aws_iam_role_policy.opal_ticket_api_ddb and -target=module.opal_ticket_api.aws_lambda_function.this. The data source needs no -target of its own. ONE plan carrying both is NOT enough to force the order: grep of main.tf finds no depends_on, and the Lambda references the role, not the policy, so Terraform has no edge from the policy to the function. The pair must be two scoped applies in sequence: (1) the policy target, then read back the statement with get-role-policy; (2) the Lambda target, after the upload of the zip to the key is the LATEST version, with no other write to that key between the upload and the plan.
terraform_note.c_order: GRANT BEFORE CODE. The check in lambda_function.py reads irpt-requests and FAILS CLOSED with a 503 when the read is denied, so a Lambda that carries the code without the statement refuses every client filing.
terraform_note.c_anything_else_in_the_diff: NONE. The diff holds only the three named items: the data source (with its comment), the IrptRequestsInputOwnerRead statement (the one-character edit of the closing bracket of the existing statement list is part of that hunk), and IRPT_REQUESTS_TABLE in the Lambda environment. CHANGELOG.json in the same directory differs between base and trunk (a 2026-10-12 deploy entry written by the release process); it is not Terraform and is not in any plan.
terraform_note.pin: NOT PINNED TO A VERSION (as the release-28 record noted): the artifact data source resolves the key's latest version at plan time, so the plan applies whatever version is latest on ticket-center/opal-ticket-api.zip. The release apply must follow its own upload with no other write to that key.
